registers.revision_note: Byte-packed: HIGH byte = meter location, LOW byte = meter type. registers.name: Generator charging switch
registers.description: BIT00: Generator charging period 1 switch, 0 off, 1 on, default 0 BIT01: Generator charging period 2 switch, 0 off, 1 on, default 0
registers.revision_note: Bit-per-period switch, all six bits documented. Six independent period enables: BIT00 period 1 .. BIT05 period 6, each 0=off 1=on, default 0. BIT06~15 reserved, default 0. PROVENANCE: this register's table is split across a PDF page break in the source document. Earlier extraction captured only the first half of the table and therefore saw BIT00 and BIT01 alone, which is why bits 2-5 were previously shipped as inferred-by-stride with an asterisk. The user supplied the continuation page, which names BIT02 period 3, BIT03 period 4, BIT04 period 5 and BIT05 period 6 explicitly, plus 'BIT06~15: reserved, default 0'. All six enables are now ATTESTED by the document, not inferred; the asterisks and the UNCONFIRMED banner have been dropped. This also settles the earlier contradiction: the register had been carrying a flat value_map {0: Disabled, 1: Enabled} harvested from Tauri's generatorChargingSwitch valueMap. That flat map is a known harvest artifact of single-bit UI toggles (43707 timeOfUseV2Switch carries the same bogus map from the same harvester yet is field-proven to be twelve independent bits), and the document's per-bit table supersedes it. WRITE: the same source page carries an explicit read-modify-write instruction, verbatim: 'Operation instructions for writing to BTIxx: The host computer first reads the current value of this register, changes the value of the corresponding BIT based on the current value as needed, and then writes;' A bare word write would silently switch off every other generator charging period, so 43815 must be merged, never overwritten.
